content.text: Section 24 is fully responsive and I have checked every cross-reference (§ 9 termination, § 13.3 licence transfer, § 30.5 successors, § 29.2 notices) for conflicting language. No redline is warranted.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 sits at our preferred position. § 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets without Vendor consent (prompt notice only). § 24.2 blocks Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by its own change of control without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and restricts assignment to a direct competitor. § 24.3 applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld standard to other assignments. § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on our change of control, and § 9 contains no change-of-control termination trigger (§ 9.2 is insolvency-based with a carve-out for lawful reorganization). Cross-references are consistent: § 13.3 carries licence rights to a permitted assignee and § 30.5 recognises a permitted successor as an enforcing person. Two minor points short of ideal preferred wording, noted only and not redlined: the competitor bar is limited to a "direct" competitor and is qualified by "without Customer's consent" — that gate is ours to control, so it operates as flexibility in our favour rather than a gap.
